reader.requirement: At --std 85, a table element (the OCCURS subject or an item subordinate to it) may be referenced by indexing only through an index-name declared in an INDEXED BY phrase of an OCCURS clause in that item's own hierarchy (with §1985:IV.4.4.2 and IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR3); a table with no INDEXED BY cannot be indexed or SEARCHed, and the index-name has no other data description.

edition-consulted.switches: the 1985 subscript SHAPE (index-name optionally +/- integer; refuses a 2002 arithmetic-expression subscript such as I1 + N with COBOL0900)
ConstructRegistry subscript-arithmetic-expression-2002: a non-integer subscript data-name is refused below 2002

reader.edition-search: The association screen itself (ScreenIndexNameAssociation, DeclaredInHierarchy) has no edition test; grep of SubscriptBinder.cs for DialectLevel/CobolVersion/ConstructRegistry/EditionContext finds only ScreenCobol85SubscriptDataNames (lines 143, 151). The 1985-only arms on the path govern subscript shape, a sibling rule, and do not change the association answer.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the association rule is the same at every edition; the subscript shape around an index-name is narrower at 1985 (no data-name increment), which is SR5/SR6 of IV.4.3.8.2.3, not this rule
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf11_01 (legal indexing) and g85_bf11_02 (another table's index-name refused); not exercised: SEARCH of a table with no INDEXED BY, subordinate-item indexing in two dimensions, an index-name also declared as data, an index data item as a subscript

probes.printed: B 6 C / D 7 / Z / FOUND Y AT 2 (exit 0)
probes.expected: subordinate F1(I1), two-dimension H1(I1,J1), I1+1, second index-name I1B, I1B-1/J1-2, ODO table F2(K2), SEARCH with its own index all accepted and correct

probes.printed: error COBOL1961: 'E2' subscripted by the index-name 'I1', which is not in the INDEXED BY phrase of any OCCURS clause in this item's hierarchy
probes.expected: refused: E2 has no INDEXED BY

probes.printed: two COBOL1961 errors: E1 by I2, F2 by I1
probes.expected: refused: index-names crossed between tables, including a subordinate item

probes.printed: error COBOL2075: SEARCH E1: the OCCURS clause of 'E1' has no INDEXED phrase
probes.expected: refused: SEARCH references the table by indexing, so INDEXED BY is required

probes.printed: error COBOL2692: 'I1' names two types of user-defined word (index-name and data-name)
probes.expected: refused: the index-name is not defined elsewhere

probes.printed: error COBOL0844: item 'X1', an index data item ... is not a numeric operand
probes.expected: refused: an index data item is not an index-name and cannot index (1985 subscripts are integer, integer data-name or index-name)

probes.printed: --std 85: error COBOL0900 ... the arithmetic-expression subscript I1 + N; --std 2023: prints C
probes.expected: 1985 refuses an index-name incremented by a data-name; 2023 admits it

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR13  (5.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR13

reader.notes: The rule is enforced by the one association screen on every subscripted reference (by declaration identity, walking the item's parents) plus SEARCH's own INDEXED check and the user-word kind screen. Diagnostics cite §2023 rules, not the 1985 text.

refuter.evidence: Probes --std 85: r3mix (outer INDEXED BY I1, inner OCCURS with no INDEXED BY, H1 (I1, 3) and H1 (3, 2)) exit 0 '6 8' (correct: mixed index/literal subscripts, the inner level is subscripted, not indexed); r3mixbad H1 (I1, J2) with J2 of another table refused COBOL1961; r3qual F1 (I1 OF T1) refused COBOL0900 (an index-name 'cannot be associated with any data hierarchy', so not qualifiable at 1985); r3dup two tables INDEXED BY I1 refused COBOL6863 citing §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR14; r3move MOVE I1 TO N refused COBOL1637 (index-name is not data). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR13  (5.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR13'; 'OK  §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR14  (5.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR14'.
